text:
The fault is most likely in the PMOS load M2. Its diode-connected gm sets the output pole, and f3dB ≈ gm2/(2π·C_L). Its sensitivity (+9.4% for +20%) is the largest of the two devices, and it is the only one whose value sets the output-pole gm directly. The measured values fit that picture: gm2 ≈ 2.83 × 580 µA ≈ 1.6 mS, which gives a pole near 520 MHz with 500 fF load, close to the measured 648 MHz. The gain (about 4.2 V/V) and GBW (2.73 GHz) still pass, so the shortfall is in the output pole rather than the gain stage. M2's bias point is also consistent with its size (gm/Id ≈ 2.8, Vov ≈ 0.62 V), so the likely corruption is M2's width or length being too small or too long for the target pole. M1 is second because its +7% sensitivity is also positive but it sets gm1, which mainly drives GBW, and GBW passes.
